title: lesser antilles regional airlines overview
content:
Airline Hub(s) Key Destinations in Lesser Antilles
Air Antilles Pointe-à-Pitre (PTP) Martinique, St. Barts, St. Martin
LIAT Antigua (ANU) Barbados, Dominica, Grenada, St. Lucia, St. Vincent, Tortola
Winair Sint Maarten (SXM) Saba, St. Eustatius, St. Barts, Antigua, Dominica
Caribbean Airlines Trinidad (POS) Grenada, Barbados, St. Lucia, St. Vincent, Antigua
SVG Air St. Vincent (SVD) Grenadines, Barbados, St. Lucia
Mustique Airways St. Vincent Grenadines, Barbados, St. Lucia
Divi Divi Air Curaçao Bonaire, Aruba
EZ Air Bonaire, Curaçao Aruba, Bonaire, Curaçao, Saba, Statia
Air Caraïbes Guadeloupe, Martinique St. Martin, St. Lucia, intra-French Caribbean
1. Air Antilles (Guadeloupe-based) Main Hub: Pointe-à-Pitre (PTP), Guadeloupe Key Destinations: Fort-de-France (Martinique), Saint-Barthélemy (St. Barts), Saint-Martin (Grand Case, French side), Cayenne (French Guiana, occasionally), Santo Domingo (Dominican Republic, seasonal) Notes: Strong focus on French Caribbean connectivity. 2. LIAT (Leeward Islands Air Transport) – Antigua-based Main Hub: V.C. Bird International Airport (ANU), Antigua Key Destinations: Antigua, Barbados, Dominica, Grenada, St. Kitts, St. Lucia, St. Vincent, Tortola Notes: Historically the backbone of Eastern Caribbean travel. Currently restructuring but still operating limited routes. 3. Winair (Windward Islands Airways) (Sint Maarten-based) Main Hub: Princess Juliana International Airport (SXM), Sint Maarten Key Destinations: Saba, St. Eustatius, St. Barthélemy, St. Kitts, Antigua, Tortola (BVI), Dominica Notes: Famous for the world’s shortest commercial runway at Saba. 4. Caribbean Airlines (Trinidad & Tobago-based, but serves Lesser Antilles) Main Hubs: Port of Spain (POS), Trinidad; Piarco International Key Destinations in Lesser Antilles: Grenada, Barbados, St. Lucia, St. Vincent, Antigua Notes: Connects the southern Lesser Antilles with Trinidad and Guyana. 5. SVG Air (St. Vincent & the Grenadines) Main Hub: Argyle International Airport (SVD), St. Vincent Key Destinations: Grenadines (Bequia, Canouan, Mustique, Union Island), Barbados, St. Lucia Notes: Essential for small-island hops in the Grenadines. 6. Mustique Airways (St. Vincent & the Grenadines) Main Hub: St. Vincent Key Destinations: Grenadines (private charters and scheduled flights) Barbados St. Lucia Notes: Popular with luxury travelers heading to Mustique. 7. Divi Divi Air (Curaçao-based, Dutch Caribbean) Main Hub: Curaçao International Airport Key Destinations: Bonaire Aruba Notes: Small commuter airline, vital for Dutch Caribbean links. 8. Z Air / EZ Air (Dutch Caribbean) Main Hubs: Bonaire & Curaçao Key Destinations: Aruba Bonaire Curaçao St. Eustatius Saba Notes: Expanding regional network in the Dutch Caribbean. 9. Air Caraïbes (French Caribbean, Guadeloupe/Martinique) Main Hubs: Pointe-à-Pitre (Guadeloupe), Fort-de-France (Martinique) Key Destinations in Lesser Antilles: Guadeloupe Martinique St. Martin St. Lucia Notes: Also operates long-haul flights to Paris.

title: lesser antilles inter-island ferry connections
content:
Hub / Island Group Operator(s) Routes / Destinations Notes
French Antilles (Guadeloupe, Dominica, Martinique, St. Lucia) L’Express des Îles Pointe-à-Pitre (Guadeloupe) ↔ Roseau (Dominica) ↔ Fort-de-France (Martinique) ↔ Castries (St. Lucia) High-speed catamarans; backbone of French Antilles ferry travel
Guadeloupe (Les Saintes, Marie-Galante) CTM Deher, Val’Ferry, Express des Îles Pointe-à-Pitre ↔ Les Saintes (Terre-de-Haut); Pointe-à-Pitre ↔ Marie-Galante Frequent daily service; popular day trips
St. Maarten / St. Martin hub Anguilla Ferry, Voyager, Great Bay Express, The Edge, Makana Marigot ↔ Anguilla; Philipsburg ↔ St. Barts; Philipsburg ↔ Saba; Philipsburg ↔ St. Eustatius St. Maarten is the northern ferry hub; very frequent Anguilla service
St. Kitts & Nevis ↔ Sint Maarten Makana Ferry Basseterre (St. Kitts) ↔ Philipsburg (Sint Maarten), sometimes via Statia/Saba Several sailings weekly; ~4–6 hrs; alternative to short flights
St. Kitts ↔ Nevis Sea Bridge, Caribe Queen, MV Mark Twain Basseterre (St. Kitts) ↔ Charlestown (Nevis) Frequent daily commuter ferries; 45 min crossing
St. Vincent & the Grenadines Bequia Express, Admiralty Transport, Jaden Sun, Mustique Co. Kingstown ↔ Bequia, Mustique, Canouan, Mayreau, Union Island Lifeline for Grenadines; multiple daily sailings
Grenada ↔ Carriacou / Petite Martinique Osprey Lines St. George’s (Grenada) ↔ Hillsborough (Carriacou) ↔ Petite Martinique Daily fast ferry; ~90 min crossing
Trinidad & Tobago TTIT (Trinidad & Tobago Inter-Island Transport) Port of Spain (Trinidad) ↔ Scarborough (Tobago) Fast ferries (2.5 hrs) and cargo ferries; very busy route
Dominica ↔ Guadeloupe / Martinique L’Express des Îles Roseau ↔ Pointe-à-Pitre; Roseau ↔ Fort-de-France Key link for Dominica post-hurricane recovery
Virgin Islands (USVI ↔ BVI) Native Son, Road Town Fast Ferry, Smith’s Ferry, Inter-Island Boat Services St. Thomas ↔ Tortola; St. Thomas ↔ Virgin Gorda; St. John ↔ Tortola Frequent commuter ferries; vital for tourism and locals

title: A concise global overview of major hurricane / typhoon / cyclone / monsoon seasons by region
content:
Summary of Global Peaks: May–November: Northern Hemisphere tropical cyclones. November–April: Southern Hemisphere cyclones and monsoons. June–September: Dominant global wet season due to Northern Hemisphere monsoons.

Tropical cyclone (hurricane / typhoon / cyclone) seasons

Region Local name Main season Peak months
North Atlantic (Caribbean, Gulf of Mexico, US East Coast) Hurricanes June – November August – October
Eastern Pacific (off Mexico) Hurricanes May – November July – September
Western Pacific (Philippines, Japan, Taiwan, China) Typhoons Year-round (main: May – November) July – October
North Indian Ocean (India, Bangladesh, Myanmar) Cyclones April – June & October – December May, November
Southwest Indian Ocean (Madagascar, East Africa) Cyclones November – April January – March
Australian region (northern Australia, PNG) Cyclones November – April February – March
South Pacific (Fiji, Tonga, Samoa) Cyclones November – April January – March

Monsoon seasons

Region Monsoon / Name Main period Notes
South Asia (India, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal) Southwest Monsoon June – September Primary wet season for the Indian subcontinent.
Southeast Asia (Thailand, Vietnam, Philippines, Malaysia) Southwest Monsoon May – October Wet season driven by monsoon winds.
East Asia (China, Korea, Japan) Meiyu / Baiu / Changma June – July Early summer rainy season.
West Africa (Sahel, Nigeria, Ghana) West African Monsoon May – October Wet season due to ITCZ movement.
Northern Australia Wet season / Monsoon November – April Overlaps with cyclone season.
